newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Postal Service says Northeast volume surges.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Postal Service says Northeast volume surges.

text.p: The U.S. Postal Service said Friday that mail and parcel volume has surged in the Northeast during the strike at United Parcel Service and that it was adding Sunday deliveries to cope with the increase.

The Postal Service said it has also taken steps to keep mail delivery current in the New England states and upstate New York through the upcoming first weekend of the strike, which started just after midnight on Monday.

Express Mail and Priority Mail were running at 75 percent above normal levels for this time of the year, the Postal Service said. The volume for packages was running 25 percent above normal, the Postal Service said.
Many larger post offices in New England and upstate New York will be delivering parcels in all three mail classes on Sunday, it said.

This will prevent any backlog of parcels on Monday and keep the mail current according to delivery service standards, the Postal Service said. Normally, only Express Mail is delivered on Sundays and holidays.

The Postal Service said it was setting some limits to adapt to the strike, including limiting the number of parcels mailed to four per customer per visit and setting appointments for customers with more than four parcels.

Negotiators for striking Teamsters and UPS resumed talks Friday after 10-1/2 hours of talks Thursday produced little progress. The Clinton administration again urged the two sides to settle. The strike has crippled Atlanta-based UPS, the world's largest package delivery company.
